commits.message: A lifecycle arrives and leaves through a glyph transition too (rich-animation-42lg.s91)

TextInput's caret blinks on the frame's time (rich-animation-42lg.31p) (#495)

* TextInput's caret blinks on the frame's time, restarted by each key (rich-animation-42lg.31p)

A frame now hands what it draws the time it is drawn for, as
RenderOptions.frameTime: the host's time for a renderable view, the
timeline's for a view on it, from one function (frameTime in core/view.ts)
that drawView and App.frameTime share. A widget lives across frames and is
never rebuilt with a t, so this is how it draws for the time without
reading a clock.

KeyEvent carries the time it was heard on that same clock; TextInput keeps
the last one and draws its caret from the blink restarted there, lit for
half a second and dark for half. The caret cell is stamped with its next
flip, so App wakes at the flip and not between. Reduced motion holds it
lit, a paused timeline holds it still, and a print draws it lit.

* The caret restarts its blink on focus, a click, and a key the field handles (rich-animation-42lg.31p)

Review of #495: a field Tab moved focus to, or a click placed the cursor
in, could show no caret for up to half a second, and a key the field passed
on restarted the blink and repainted. Every event a widget hears now carries
its time on the frame's clock (WidgetMouseEvent.time, WidgetFocusEvent.time;
focus(time)/blur(time)), stamped by the router and the focus manager from
the same frameTime keys already use. TextInput restarts from focus, a
mouse_down, and a key it stops.

The blink runs away from its restart in either direction of time, so a
timeline played backwards also finds the caret lit just after a key.
